Commentary.Commentary: Now then, the target is a huge one! Over 100 overs to go. South Africa will have to bat out of their skin if they are to chase this down. Pakistan on the other hand, will back themselves to pick all the 10 wickets. The pitch is not that bad so if you apply yourself, you can score big.

For South Africa, Linde and Maharaj were the pick! Especially the former who ended with a fifer. However, they were excellent yesterday but today their bowlers looked quite flat. The wicket also did not offer a lot but they will still be disappointed they took a little too much time to dismiss the bowling all-rounders.

There were decent stands between Rizwan and Ashraf, then the former with Hasan Ali and Nauman. He was the mainstay as he went onto score his maiden ton. His innings has probably batted South Africa out of the game.

370 is what South Africa have to chase to level the series! Probably a little too much right? Rizwan's innings is probably going to be the one which will help Pakistan win the series. South Africa had their chances when they had Pakistan at 76 for 5. At that time, it seemed like the max Pakistan would set was 250. However, the story of the series continues, the lower-order of the hosts' line-up continues to frustrate the visitors.

OUT! AFRIDI HAS BEEN CASTLED!  FIFER FOR LINDE! First in Tests and that is exactly what he was got on for. One wicket left and he was given an opportunity to pick it and he gets it. The arm ball on off, this does not turn. Afridi goes back and plays for the turn into him. It beats the outsied edge and clips the bail of the off pole. Afridi is waiting there. The umpire takes it upstairs to check but replays show it is fine! PAKISTAN HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 298!
The umpire is not sure whether Afridi is cleaned up or has de Kock knocked the bails off and they have gone upstairs.
On middle, this is worked to mid on.
This lands outside off and turns back in. Nicely left by Afridi.
A single now as this is eased down to long on.
Floats it up on middle, it is pushed to mid on.
On middle, this is pushed back to the bowler.
Linde is on! Can he get his fifth!
Shorter again, Afridi is solid in defense.
Shorter and on middle again, this is defended off the back foot.
Another one on middle, Afridi stays back and keeps it out.
On middle, this is kept out.
Shorter and outside off, Afridi looks to pull but misses.
SIX! Smoked! Take that says Afridi! This is fuller and on off, Shaheen clears his front leg and hammers it over the long off fence for a biggie. So he might have some fun here.

DRINKS! Pakistan going along strongly! The only thing which has gone South Africa's way is Nauman's wicket. Will the misery for them continue or will they take the last wicket quickly? We will find out in a bit.
A dot to end which means Shaheen will be on strike! Shorter and on the body, Rizwan looks to pull but misses.
Another bumper, Rizwan pulls it but to mid-wicket. Another dot.
On the shorter side, this is nudged towards mid-wicket for no runs.
Short again, Rizwan gets on top of the bounce and pulls it to mid-wicket.
One more short one, this is pulled towards fine leg for a single.
Nortje bowls this one short and on the body, Rizwan pulls but to deepish square leg.
A short one to welcome Afridi! He lets it go to the keeper.
Shaheen Afridi walks out to bat!

OUT! TAKEN! Heartbreak for Nauman as he falls 5 short of his first half ton! He deserved it. Showed great character but is done in by the short ball ploy. He looks to pull again but gets a top edge. It seems like it would land safe in the mid-wicket region but Elgar there runs in, dives and takes a good catch. Can they now take the last wicket quickly?
A slower short ball, Ali looks to pull but misses it altogether.
On off, it is pushed towards cover for one.
On off, Rizwan keeps it out nicely.
FOUR! Deft! Length and outside off, Rizwan waits for it and then opens the face of the bat. Guides it through backward point for a boundary.
On middle, this is worked to mid-wicket.
FOUR! Over the keeper now! This is a sensible stroke! One more short ball, this is on middle. Nauman plays the upper cut and it goes over the keeper for a boundary.
FOUR! Into the 40s! This time connects with the pull shot. It goes behind square on the leg side for a boundary.
Another quick bumper! Ali looks to pull but misses.
One mroe short one, Ali moves out of the way this time.
Short and on middle, Ali pulls but finds the man at square leg.
On the middle pole, Rizwan keeps it out. End of a good over for Pakistan.
This one stays low! Outside off, does not bounce. Rizwan fails to put bat on ball.
Angled into the pads, MR works it to mid-wicket.
Back of a length and on off, Rizwan defends it onto the ground.
FOUR! 350 is the lead now! Back-to-back boundaries! This is right off the middle. On a length and around off, Rizwan strokes it through covers and the ball races away to the fence.

EDGY FOUR! Runs coming thick and fast now for Pakistan! Length and around off, Rizwan hangs his bat out away from the body. It goes off the inside edge past the off pole and down to the fine leg fence.
FOUR! Dragged wide! Nauman is now oozing in confidence as he nears his first Test fifty! The sweep is out, it is with the turn and he hits it behind square on the leg side. Boundary.
Tossed up on off, Ali keeps it out.
Shorter and outside off, Rizwan slaps it towards cover for one.
Good shot from Nauman now! On off, this is pushed wide of mid off for one.

Calls for a run and gets it! There it is! A ton for Rizwan! His first in Tests! What a solid knock this is! All of his teammates are out on the balcony applauding the effort. What a special moment for him. He walked out when his side was under pressure and has excelled. He has probably batted his team in a posiiton from where it is very difficult for them to lose. He gets there by pushing this with the turn towards cover for one. He might look to up the ante now.
Steps out but does not get to the pitch of the ball! Rizwan defends it nicely.
Onto 99 now! Shorter and on middle, this is pulled down to fine leg. Rizwan also keeps strike.
FOUR! In the gap and he moves onto 98! 2 runs short of what will be his first Test ton! It is short and into the pads, Rizwan pulls it behind square on the leg side and bags a boundary.
Angled into the middle pole, this is pushed back to the bowler.
On off, Rizwan pushes it to mid off.
Angled into the pads once again, this is worked to mid-wicket.
Angled into the pads, Rizwan works it to mid-wicket.
Full and flat, around off, well defended.
Full again, looped up, outside off, pushed to the off side.
Looped up, around off, well defended.
Looped up, outside off, well blocked out.
Around off, spinning down, Nauman lunges and watchfully keeps it out, in front of short leg.
Full and around leg, blocked in front of short leg. Gets it past him and earns a single.
Full and around middle, Nauman keeps it down, in front of short leg.
Another forward defense is on offer.
Full again, well kept out.
Full and around off, pushed towards cover.
Works this though mid-wicket for a single. The lead ticks on to 330.
Full and flat, around middle, watchfully defended.
Around off, watchfully kept out.
Around middle, well blocked in front of short leg.
SIX! HUMONGOUS! That is great connection. It is not a small boundary either. Full and around off, Nauman gets down and mows a slog sweep over mid-wicket. Ali moves to 32, in a stand of 62.
Quicker one, outside off, kept out solidly.
On middle, wristed through mid-wicket. Happy to take the single this time.
Looped up, around middle, driven back to the bowler.
A touch shorter, around middle, Ali goes back and plays it in front of short leg.
Similar ball, same reaction.
Full, around off, spinning in slowly, Nauman lunges and keeps it out.
Full and around middle, well defended.
Around middle, watchfully defended.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover for a single.
Full and around off, well blocked out.
Down the leg side, Ali sweeps it behind square leg for a couple. 250 UP FOR PAKISTAN. Lead by 321.
Outside off, driven towards point. Rizwan wants the single but is sent back.
Full agin, driven again, through the covers, along the ground this time. Gets a single, wanted the second, moves to 90.
FOUR! 50-STAND IS BROUGHT UP! Struck magnificently. Full and outside off, Rizwan stays leg side of the delivery and lofts it over cover.
Full and around middle, flicked towards deep mid-wicket. No single taken.
Full again, nice, compact defense.
Around off, solidly defended.

FOUR! Excellent work by George Linde in the deep though. Full and around off, Nauman swings it towards mid-wicket. Linde gets across to his right, dives and pushes the ball back in play. Two runs taken. But then, the umpires take it upstairs, to check the fielding effort. From one angle, it does seem like when Linde is pushing the ball away, his right knee is touching the ropes. Boundary signalled.
Around off, well defended.
Outside off, pushed towards cover.

EDGED, FOUR! Runs are flowing now. The stand moves to 43 and Nauman has made 20 of those. The lead is now 310. Full and outside off, Nauman looks to drive but the ball takes the outside edge and goes past first slip, to his left, to the third man fence.
FOUR! Fine shot. On a length, outside off, Rizwan punches this through the covers. Not a soul moves. 10 from the over!
Around off, watchfully defended.

Is that a missed run out? Yes, perhaps! A short ball, around middle, MR pulls this through mid-wicket again. Nauman thinks it is just a single as there is a fielder in the deep but Rizwan calls him through for the second. Keshav Maharaj returns a good throw to the bowler with Ali halway down. Nortje collects, looks to push it onto the stumps, but misses! Replays show that Nauman had made it but his bat was in the air! He was plonking it in. Rizwan moves to 81.
FOUR! THE LEAD GOES PAST 300! Short ball, around off, Rizwan gets on top of the bounce and pull it all along the carpet through mid-wicket. The stand is worth 33 now.
A short ball, around middle, Rizwan swivels and pulls it towards deep backward square leg. Does not take the single.
A bouncer, around middle, Rizwan ducks.
SIX! HAMMERED! There comes the first sign of going for quick runs. Full and down the leg side, Nauman gets down and sweeps it powerfully over square leg!
Slowly looped up, outside off, watchfully blocked out.
Full and around off, eased down to long off for a single. The lead moves to 290.
Around off, blocked out watchfully.
Tossed up, outside off, Rizwan jumps out and drives but finds Temb Bavuma at cover.
Fuller, around middle, driven towards mid on.
A bouncer on middle, ducked under.
Banged in short, around off, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Around off, MR is able to rock back to defend.
Back of a length, around off, well defended.
Fuller, around off, well defended.
On a length, outside off, pushed towards cover.

Welcome back. 300 of the lead for Pakistan. Century for Rizwan. 5-fer for Linde. These are the things to look forward to as a fan. The players are back onto the field. It will be Anrich Nortje to Mohammad Rizwan first up.
... DAY 4, SESSION 2 ...

What's coming up after Lunch? Quick runs? Possible declaration? All out? Don't think runs or time make any difference now. In fact, South Africa will start to believe that the longer Pakistan bat, the lesser they have to bat themselves in the final innings. Join us back at 12.40 pm local (0740 GMT) for the second session. 62 overs left in the day. How much will the Proteas have to face?

Bowling in such conditions is so tough. It is not just the pitch. It is the fact that you have dismissed half the side quickly but the lower half tends to show better application than the top half. South Africa managed to pick 5 wickets for 76 but since then, have conceded 141 runs for just 3 more. It is the irritation which sets in and later leads to frustration. Fielding is not helping either. Had the catches been taken, the Proteas might have well been batting by now, chasing somewhere under 200. Instead, they are waiting for a possible declaration now. The spinners have taken 7 out of the 8 wickets to fall but the grit and application from Pakistan is admirable. Linde has gone in too much with the leg-side line and conceded a few runs in the process. But Maharaj has bowled beautifully.

88/2 in 34 overs. Session belongs to Pakistan. And with that, the game as well. What a knock from Rizwan. He started the day with Hasan Ali and has shepherded the tail nicely. Off the 88 runs, he has scored 45. The hosts will be eyeing to take the lead towards 300 but one feels this much is enough too. Just 4 sessions left in the game and to score 75 on an average in each, with the pitch wearing out, is going to be very difficult.
Outside off, Ali looks to defend but the ball spin away, takes the outside edge and goes to the left of slip. Nauman wants two and Rizwan agrees. LUNCH ON DAY 4, PAKISTAN LEAD BY 288!
Full once more, pushed towards mid off.
Full again, this is watchfully defended.
Landed outside off, on the rough, too much spin, Nauman looks to defend but misses. The ball goes off his pads to silly point. Appeals all around but nothing in it.
Outside off, pushed with soft hands towards cover. Rizwan calls for two but there is just one available.
Fuller and around off, driven straight to cover.
A short ball, around middle, Nauman fends it down the track.
Another bouncer, ducked under again.
A short ball, around off, angling across, NA takes his bat away from the line.
A bouncer now, Ali ducks properly under it.
FOUR! Nicely played! A length ball, around middle, Nauman helps it uppishly, but well wide of Keshav Maharaj at square leg, to his right. The ball races away.
Slower ball, short in length, angling away, Nauman looks to cut but misses.

Tossed up, outside off, NA comes forward and drives it nicely through the covers. Mid off gets across to his right and the single is taken, but forcefully. Nauman wanted it, Rizwan didn't. He doesn't like the idea of Nauman facing Nortje.
Fuller, around leg, Ali lunges to block but the ball goes past his bat, hits his pad and lobs towards backward square leg.
Down the leg side, left alone.
Looped up, outside off, Nauman stretches to defend.
Landed outside off, spins a mile down the leg side! Left alone.

Rizwan shapes up for the sweep but he telegraphs it. So Linde drops it short and outside off. But the adjustment is quick and Rizwan immediately cuts it through cover for a single. The lead is now 280.
Change of ends for George Linde. 18-9-29-4 so far.
On a good length,around middle, Ali rises with the bounce and pats it towards cover.
Outside off, pushed through the covers for a run.
On a length, outside off, Rizwan plays a loose cut and misses. No footwork there.
Outside leg, nudged towards square leg where Temba Bavuma gets to the ball but fumbles, allowing the single.
Around middle, pushed to the off side.
A bouncer to start. Around leg stump, Nauman ducks.
As expected, it is pace from the other end. Anrich Nortje is summoned. 11-6-32-0 so far.
Full and around off, pushed towards cover.
Shorter, around off, cut straight to point.
Full and around off, MR lunges to block but misses.
Full and around middle, well defended.
Outside off, spinning away, pushes towards point.
Ahh.... did that hit one of the cracks? Full, around off, Rizwan looks to defend but the ball pitches and then deviates a mile past the outside edge.
The second new ball is due now. The fourth umpire brings it out and hands it to Aleem Dar. And SOUTH AFRICA TAKE THE SECOND NEW BALL STRAIGHTAWAY.  Maharaj to continue.
The arm ball, outside off, Nauman looks to defend but misses.
Full again, around off, well defended once more.
Nicely played. Head down, reaching out, meeting the ball and exhibiting good defense.
Slowly tossed up, outside off, pushed towards Faf du Plessis at long off for a single. Rizwan moves to 70 and this stand is worth 10.
Looped up, outside off, driven straight to cover.
Tossed up, around middle, driven back to the bowler.
Quick single taken again. Full and around middle, Rizwan pushes it towards mid on and calls for a quick single. Anrich Nortje attacks the ball but then takes his eyes off at the last moment. Fumbles.
Tossed up, around middle, driven towards mid on.
Nice rotation of the strike. Ali reaches out, pushes it to the right of silly point, spots the gap and picks a run.
Fuller, round-armish, Nauman lunges to defend.
Fuller, around middle, worked through mid on for a single.
Full and around middle, Rizwan reaches out to drive it back to the bowler.
Another play and a miss. Wide outside off, no need to play but Ali still reaches out to push. Misses.
Around middle and leg, worked to the leg side.
Very full, outside off, straightening a bit, Nauman looks to push but misses.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Around middle, well blocked.
Full and around middle, watchfully defended.

FOUR BYES! Tossed up wide outside off, Rizwan gets across, looks to play an attacking sweep but misses. Quinton de Kock behind is not able to collect again. The ball races to the fence behind, bringing up 200 FOR PAKISTAN. They lead by 273.
Short and outside off, Rizwan looks to cut but misses.
Around off, driven towards short extra cover.
Outside off, Ali looks to defend but gets an outside edge, which somehow goes to the right of silly point. A single taken.
Fuller, around off, Nauman lunges to push it back.
Tossed up, outside off, well defended.
Fuller, around middle, MR pushes it towards mid on sets off for a single but then realizes that he has hit it too well. Changes the call.
The arm ball, around middle, defended to the leg side.
Fuller, around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Landed outside off, Rizwan looks to hammer it through the covers but misses.
Fuller and around middle, driven back to Linde who gets hit on the left hand again.
Outside off, punched towards sweeper cover. No run taken. Interesting. Time for some shots then?
Big turn again, sharp one at that, Ali looks to defend but misses and is hit on the pads.
Outside off, watchfully defended this time.

MISSES THE STUMPS! Big turn. Full and outside off, landing on the rough, Nauman looks to drive. But the ball whizzes in, takes the inside edge and scoots past leg stump. Ali has no idea where the ball is and looks for the single but is quickly sent back, as backward square leg gets across to the ball.
Short and outside off, spinning away, cut through the covers for a single.
Fuller, around middle, driven back to the bowler.
Short and outside off, pushed towards point.
Keshav Maharaj returns. 31-3-99-3 so far.
Full and around off, pushed away from his body, towards cover.
Nauman Ali walks in at number 10, replacing Yasir. How much more can Pakistan add?

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! The 53-run stand is finally broken. Two people will be very much disappointed with the shot and result. Yasir himself and Mohammad Rizwan. All throughout the morning, Rizwan has been telling Yasir to be careful with the cut shot. But from Yasir's point of view, this was a loose ball. Short and outside off, there to be cut. He looks to do so but only manages to get a thick outside edge to Quinton de Kock. There is barely an appeal and Shah walks off. End of a crucial contribution. Pakistan lead by 267. Linde has 4 now.
Around middle and leg, pushed back to the bowler.
Fuller, around middle, pushed towards mid off.
Thrown up, outside off, a touch wide, driven through the covers for a single.
Full and around leg, Rizwan looks to sweep but misses.
Short and outside off, cut towards point. Yasir sets off for the single seeing the fielder deep but Rizwan sends him back. There looked like a single being on offer though.
Outside off, placed with an open bat face towards point for a single.
Kicks off a length, from outside off, MR is surprised but manages to keep it down.
Outside off, pushed towards the off side.

FOUR! Nicely played. Runs are coming quite easily for Rizwan and Pakistan now. 50-RUN STAND IS UP BETWEEN THESE TWO. Rizwan moves to 60 as well. Short and around off, Rizwan latches onto the length and pulls it through mid-wicket.
Outside off, blocked to the off side.
Wiaan Mulder is back into the attack. 6-1-11-0 so far. Quinton de Kock is upto the stumps for him.
Short and outside off, Yasir backs away, looking to cut but mistimes it towards cover.
Full and around middle, well defended.

Excellent work by Anrich Nortje. Another one down the leg side, Rizwan paddles it to the right of leg slip this time. The ball races away towards the ropes but Nortje rushes across to his right from fine leg, gets to the ball, bends and pushes the ball back in. Three runs taken. The lead is now 261.
Very full, around middle, MR sweeps it powerfully. The ball goes off the toe end of the bat and is half-stopped by leg slip. Rizwan wants the single but is sent back.
Around middle, blocked back to the bowler.

FOUR! Short and outside off, Rizwan chops it away behind point. Kagiso Rabada is in hot pursuit from deep point, races to his left, slides across, gets to the ball, tries to push it away but deflects it into the ropes instead. 50 FOR RIZWAN. Another crucial knock, shepherding the tail once more.
Another one down the leg side, paddled towards short fine leg for a quick single. The stand moves to 40 and Rizwan moves to 49.

Down the leg side again, Yasir looks to do what Rizwan did last ball but plays a bit too early. So instead of fine leg, the ball goes to deep square leg, off the toe end of the bat. A single still results.
Full and down the leg side, Rizwan reaches out and sweeps it to the left of short fine leg for a run.
Fuller, around off, looped up, worked wide of long on for a single.
Outside off, pushed towards cover.
Tossed up, outside off, Yasir winds up, looking to swing, but mistimes it towards mid on.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Full again, eased towards cover. Wants a single but is sent back.
Full and around off, pushed to the off side.
Full and around off, well  blocked out.
On middle and leg, watchfully defended.
FOUR BYES! More runs. THE LEAD IS NOW 250. Full and down the leg side, Rizwan looks to sweep but misses. Quinton de Kock is not tidy enough behind the stumps and the ball races to the fine leg fence.
Nicely bowled by Maharaj, plenty of flight, nice dip, around off, watchfully kept out.
Full and around middle, well defended.
On middle and leg, blocked down towards mid on.
Outside off, Rizwan leans and pushes this through the covers for a single.
Action replay of the previous delivery.
Full on middle, well defended.
FOUR! Down the leg side, Yasir just uses the pace of the delivery and plays it nicely, to the left of leg slip, along the ground and into the fine leg fence. Moves to 21 in a stand of 31.
Full on middle once more, blocked out.
Full again, on middle, defended back down the pitch.
Full and around leg, Shah looks to defend but the ball pitches and then spins away, taking the outside edge, going past first slip, to his right. Two runs taken. The lead moves to 241.

Bowler killer, umpire killer! Ahsan Raza, please take care! And Linde, you too. Full and around off, Yasir comes down the track and hammers it straight back. Linde tries to stick his right hand out but cannot catch that. The ball bursts through his hands and almost takes the umpire out, who is on the ground. The ball deflects towards mid on. It was Linde's left hand in the first innings, now, it is his right.
Tossed up, outside off, driven towards mid off for a single.

DRINKS BREAK. A good passage of play for Pakistan. They have lost just the one wicket of Hasan Ali and have added 38 runs in 16 overs. The run rate is never an issue and look at the lead - Inching closer to 250. South Africa have not done any favours on themselves by dropping catches but they need to forget that and concentrate on trying to take these remaining 3 wickets quickly. There is a lot happening on the pitch and batting is getting difficult by the moment.
Full and around middle, well defended.
The arm ball, right in line of the stumps, Rizwan is almost defeated as he looks to push though the line but manages to adjust it to push the ball through point. One run taken.
Around off, eked out past silly point for a run.
Full again, flicked wide of mid on, to his right, for a single.

Just a touch too full, around middle, pushed back down the track.

What was the noise? Short and outside off, Rizwan rocks back and looks to cut but misses. Thereis a big noise as the ball goes past the bat and South Africa start celebrating. The umpire is unmoved, so they put in an appeal. The response is a shake of the head. De Kock immediately takes the review as he is that confident. But Ultra Edge detects nothing as the ball goes past the outside edge! Review lost, but what was the noise then?
Gosh. That looked out to the naked eye. Terrific umpiring decision.

Around middle, driven towards mid on.

Fuller, around off, driven back to the bowler.
On middle and leg, watchfully defended.

Ball Tracker showed the ball to be clipping leg stump, so the review is retained but the wicket isn't.

PITCH REPORT - Mike Haysman says there are cracks around the good length area and they have gotten wider but are still hard. South Africa are yet to score 250 in this tour so far so they will not be wanting to let the hosts to get to that total. They would be eager to take the remaining wickets as quickly as possible and probably keep Pakistan to something around 220. The first hour could well be one which decides the game. Stay tuned.

Hello and welcome to the coverage of the 4th day of second Test between Pakistan and South Africa! The game is nicely poised, one can say the hosts have their noses slightly ahead but the visitors know if they get a couple of wickets quickly, they can turn the tide into their favor. The lead is now 200 and Pakistan would be eager to take it over 250 which will be a difficult chase on this wicket. Their hopes are pinned on Rizwan as he is the last recognized batsman. Can he add more 50 runs at least?
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

Right then. The Moving Day hangs in the balance slightly. Both the teams have played well and the first session of Day 4 will give us an idea as to where this Test is heading. Pakistan have a lead of 200 and they will want to pile on the lead. South Africa, on the other hand, will want to come out and remove Rizwan first and then the tail of Pakistan very quickly. So do join us for Day 4 which will begin at 0945 local (0445 GMT). Until then, cheers!

Pakistan will not be too worried about how things have gone by for them on Day 3. They did well with the ball and bundled the tail of South Africa for just 201. But, their show with the bat could have been better as, by the end of Day 3, they have lost 6 wickets. They do have a lead of 200 runs but they know that they will need some more runs on the board if they want to post a competitive total. They have Rizwan and Ali out there and will be hoping that these two can build a strong partnership and help them post a big total.

Starting off the day, the South African batters could not really cut the deficit by a lot. They tried their best to bring the deficit down but some good bowling and also some reckless running between the wickets saw them bundle up for just 201 runs and they were behind by 71 runs. Bavuma and Mulder played well but with no support from the other end, they could not do much. With the ball though, they will be happy with their exploits. They removed 6 batters and closed the day off nicely enough. The pick of the lot was definitely George Linde as he bowled very well, was economical and also snared 3 wickets. His partner in crime, Maharaj also scalped two. Overall, they have been good with the ball and will look to continue this on Day 4.

An interesting day of play comes to a close. Both the teams will be pretty pleased with how things have fared for them. They have both had their moments in the Day and at the end of the day, there seems to be no clear winner of the Day but it does seem that South Africa have their noses very slightly in front as they scalped 6 wickets in their second innings and Pakistan closed the day off with a lead of 200 runs.

... Day 3, Session 3 ...

Whereas, the South African bowlers will be gunning to come out and break this stand and scalp a few more wickets to apply more pressure on the hosts. Which team takes the final session? Join us for the same shortly.

South Africa will not be happy with how they started off the innings but they have been fairly good with the ball in hand. They started off poorly as they were not able to hang around and turn that deficit into a lead and ended their first innings by trailing by 71 runs. With the ball, they started off really well as they did not let the openers of Pakistan settle and Rabada struck when he got rid of Butt. Then, Maharaj got the better of Abid Ali and that was where we stood at the end of the second session.

An even session of play, by the looks of things now. Though, Pakistan will be the happier side of the lot as they are in the position of ascendancy at the moment. They hold all the cards close to their chest and also head into the Tea break with a good lead of 113. They started the session of nicely as they bundled the South African tail for a total of 201 and took a lead of 71 too. Then, they came out to bat and were slow to start off with. Abid and Butt did not even opened the account when Butt fell. Maharaj then got the better of Abid Ali and since then, the skipper, Azam and Azhar Ali have survived until Tea.

Floated delivery on middle, Abid pushes it to mid on.
FOUR! Nicely swept! Flighted ball on middle, Abid plays a slog sweep over square leg for a boundary.
Tossed up delivery on off, Abid defends it off the back foot.
Outside off, Azhar leaves it alone.
Length delivery on middle, Ali keeps it out.
Bouncer outside off, Ali sways away from it.
Good length ball on off, Ali looks to defend but gets hit on the thigh pad.
Back of a length on middle, Ali pushes it to mid on.
Good length delivery on off, Ali defends it to covers.

DRINKS. Pakistan would be happy with how they have started off. Yes, they have lost Butt early on but they do have a lead to their name, which with the experience of Azhar Ali and Abid Ali out there, they will hope to inflate. South Africa has bowled well so far and have kept a tight leash on the runs and will look to scalp a few quick wickets before Tea.
On middle, defended.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.

On a length and on off, Abid pushes it to the point region. The fielder decides to give it back to the keeper but de Kock was not expecting this one to come back and the ball goes to the leg side. The batters pick up two runs off overthrows.
Short and around off, pushed to the cover region.
Goes on the back foot and blocks this one out.
On middle, blocked to the leg side.
Full toss on middle, worked to the leg side for a single.
Back of a length and on off, Abid pushes this one to the mid on region.
Short of a length and on off, Abid keeps this one out well.
Pushed to the point region this time by Abid.
On off, pushed to the cover region.
Bumper on middle, Abid ducks under this well.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.

STOP THE PRESS! ABID ALI HAS FINALLY OPENED HIS ACCOUNT THIS TIME! It has taken some time but he has done it finally. He has taken 23 balls to get here as well. Shortish and outside off, Abid Ali gets on his back foot and slaps this one through backward point. Van der Dussen gives this chase and does well to pull it back before the ropes. Gets three runs, does Abid. The umpires have a look to see if this is a clean save and replays roll in and the third umpire decides that three runs will suffice.
On middle, whipped to the right of mid on for a single.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.

FOUR! Misfield from Rabada. He falls and tumbles, which allows the ball to trickle through to the ropes. Flighted and on middle, Azhar Ali gets on his knees and paddles this one to the fine leg region and a fumble from the pacer sees the Pakistanis get a boundary.
Floats and lands it on middle, Azhar pushes this to mid on.
Keshav Maharaj is coming onto bowl.
And the wait continues on. Good length and on off, Abid pushes this one to mid on. A loud and clear 'No' is heard this time as well. 22 balls. No runs for Abid.
The batsman has just blocked that from his crease.
Abid Ali hops to this back of a length delivery and taps this one to the leg side. 'No' is the call from Abid. Still waiting for a 'YES, YES, YES' from Abid, so that he can finally open his account.
Outside off on a good length, left alone by Abid.
Gets his bat across and keeps this one out, does Abid.
Short of a length and around the off pole, Abid Ali hops and blocks this one out well.
Tucked to the fielder at short mid-wicket for yet another maiden over.
Bouncer outside the off pole, Azhar does not offer any shot to this one.
On middle, tucked to the short leg fielder.
Bumper outside off, Azhar has no problems in letting this one go.
On a good length and around off, Azhar pushes this one to the cover region.
Back of a length and on off, Azhar blocks.
16 balls faced and Abid Ali has still not scored a run. On middle, tucked to the short leg fielder. A brilliant over for Rabada and the Proteas. Only one run and a wicket off this one too.
Another bouncer on middle, Abid Ali sits under this one.
Abid plays this one back towards Rabada, this time.
Bumper on middle, Abid ducks under this one.
Azhar Ali comes out and gets the first run straightaway. A short one on middle, Azhar fends this one awkwardly to the square leg region for a single.
Azhar Ali is the new batsman in.

OUT! LBW! There it is! The pressure was building too much and something was bound to give. Rabada bowls a wonderful delivery and Pakistan lose their first wicket, without registering a single run on the board. Rabada steams in and hurls across a delivery which is just behind the good length area. Lands it around off and gets it to tail back in ever-so-slightly. Butt misses his tuck away to the leg side and gets rapped on the pads. Rabada believes and so do the South African players. The umpire obliges and gets his finger up. Butt does not opt for the review as he knows this one was plumb. Just the start that the Saffas were looking for.
Blocked to the leg side this time. Yet another maiden for South Africa. Pressure is building on the hosts. Something is bound to give.
Short one on middle, Ali does well to sway away from the line of the ball.
The batsman has just blocked that from his crease.

BEATEN! Woohoooo! That is the length, Nortje. Bowls a back of a length ball around off, straigtens after hitting the deck, this time. Ali feels that he can try to block this one but the ball zips past the outside edge to de Kock.
A back of a length ball on middle, nips into the right-hander, Ali looks for the tuck away but he misses and the ball takes the pad and goes to the off side.
Dishes a back of a length ball on off, Ali taps this one to point.
The third maiden in a row. The Pakistani openers are yet to open their account in this inning so far. On a length and outside off, Butt does not have a poke at this one.
Another block offered by Imran. But this time, it is pushed to the leg side.
Butt pushes this one back towards Rabada with a straight bat.
Bouncer on middle, Butt just ducks under this one.
On a good length and outside off, tapped to the gully region.
Length and outside off, no shot offered to this one by Butt.
PLAY AND A MISS! On a length and outside off, Ali looks to drive this one but the ball whizzes past the outside edge and goes through to the keeper.
In that channel of uncertainty outside the off pole, Ali shoulders arms to this one as well.
Outside off, left alone.
Short of a length and on off, Ali looks to pull this one to the leg side but the ball takes the inside edge and hits him on the pads.
BEATEN! Beautiful delivery. A short of a length ball on off, it bounces a tad bit more as Abid misses his block and the ball fizzles to the keeper.
Anrich starts off with a length ball outside off, Abid lets it go.
Anrich Nortje to bowl from the other end.
A maiden to start off by Rabada. Another length ball on off, Butt pushes this one towards the point region.
On a good length and around off, Butt blocks this one out.
A shortish length delivery outside off, Butt hops and just lets this one be.
Outside off, left alone.
Identical to the last delivery. Butt offers the same shot this time as well. Which is basically no shot.
Rabada starts off with a good length ball outside off, Butt shoulders arms to this one.
